Front: Define precision and recall: which penalizes false positives, which penalizes false negatives?
Back: Precision = TP/(TP+FP), penalizes false positives (out of everything predicted positive, how many actually were). Recall = TP/(TP+FN), penalizes false negatives (out of everything actually positive, how many were caught). Recall has nothing to do with true negatives.

Front: Give a correctly-matched recall-priority example and a correctly-matched precision-priority example.
Back: Recall-priority: illness screening on a rare-positive dataset - missing a true case (false negative) is costlier than a false alarm, so tune to catch nearly all true positives even at the cost of more false positives. Precision-priority: a pet door recognizing only your specific cat - letting an intruder cat in (false positive) matters more than occasionally blocking your own cat (false negative), so tune to be very sure before letting anything through.

Front: Concrete case: how can a model have low loss/high accuracy but still be rejected on a metric?
Back: On a heavily imbalanced dataset (99% negative class), a model that always predicts the majority class gets low average loss and high accuracy, but recall on the minority (positive) class is 0% - it never catches a single true positive. Loss/accuracy alone can hide a metric that matters more for the task.

Front: StepLR vs. ReduceLROnPlateau: what's the actual mechanism difference?
Back: StepLR decays the learning rate by a fixed factor (gamma) at fixed, predetermined epoch intervals (step_size) - it has no awareness of training progress, just a clock. ReduceLROnPlateau is the adaptive one: it monitors a metric (e.g. validation loss) and only cuts the learning rate once that metric stops improving for a set number of epochs.

Front: Meta-lesson: what's the two-part check when using precision/recall (or any paired concept) in a worked example?
Back: Getting the formula/definition right doesn't guarantee the worked example is correctly matched to it - that's a separate check. Explicitly state which error type (FP or FN) the scenario tolerates vs. penalizes before assigning it to precision or recall, rather than pattern-matching from the topic (e.g. 'illness = critical = precision') alone.
